cards.title: Managing After-School Restraint Collapse
cards.body: Kids often vent frustration at home after a long school day. Five practical steps can help you manage this behavior effectively and support your child through the transition.

cards.title: Kids and Mental Health Beyond Comfort
cards.body: Children benefit from knowing they can share their emotional lives with trusted adults. This foundation helps them develop skills to understand and manage their inner world.

cards.title: Boomer Parents and Millennial Daughters Miscommunicate
cards.body: Loving parents and adult daughters often misunderstand each other despite their best intentions. Three everyday phrases reveal hidden emotional labor that can turn connection into conflict.

cards.title: Transform Your Adult Child-Parent Connection
cards.body: Parents who ignore boundaries or make you feel guilty can trap you in your 'child' role. These starter solutions can eliminate conflict and liberate you from unhelpful dynamics.

cards.title: Halloween Magic and Connection for Kids
cards.body: From Samhain to Day of the Dead, celebrating autumn can create special moments with your children. This year offers an opportunity to ditch cynicism and embrace seasonal magic together.

cards.title: Working Parent Logistics and School Holidays
cards.body: Working parents face a logistical nightmare balancing school schedules with work commitments. School holidays could be an opportunity to actually spend quality time with kids instead of managing constant admin.

cards.title: Accessing Family Medical History When Adopted
cards.body: People who are adopted or in care often struggle to access family medical history crucial to their own health. Not knowing can be terrifying and leave gaps in understanding important health risks.

cards.title: Saving for Kids' Future: Child Pensions
cards.body: A growing number of parents are opening pensions for their children to save £100 monthly. These accounts ensure financial security but funds won't be accessible until adulthood.

cards.title: Family Estrangement: When to Go No Contact
cards.body: One in five UK families experience permanent estrangement, making it a significant but difficult decision. Experts provide key questions to help you decide if cutting contact is right for your situation.
